title: Python SDK for ZIdentity (client.zid): where its models and keys depart from the API

prose.text: The Python SDK reaches ZIdentity as `client.zid.<service>`; its modules and methods are generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface zid`). The defects below come from how it converts keys and which model it builds from each response.

prose.label: Key conversion.
prose.text: {{form-response-camel}} Request bodies and query keys are camel-cased the same way: [[zidentity.api.query-filters:python-params-camel-cased]] and [[shared.sdk-python.request-handling:camel-rule]].

prose.label: Array responses read as one object.
prose.text: {{secrets-response-array}} {{secrets-get-builds-one}} {{secrets-list-into-object}} {{service-entitlement-builds-one}} {{service-entitlement-into-object}} The administrative read is wrapped instead: {{admin-entitlement-wrapper}}

prose.label: Groups.
prose.text: A group's source takes the values in [[zidentity.groups:source-values]]. The SDK's docstring offers a value outside them and fields the create body does not define {{divergence:group-source-manual}} {{divergence:add-group-body}}. {{membership-id-transform}}

checks.do: Whether code reads `results_total` or `next_link` from a Python list object; they are always None, so count `records` or use the response object's paging.
Whether an empty result from `get_api_client_secret` or `get_service_entitlement` comes from the parsing defect rather than the tenant, by reading the raw response body.
For a JWKS client created through Python, whether the stored client shows the JWKS URL, since the SDK sends it under `clientJwKsUrl`.

form-response-camel.statement: Before a ZIdentity model such as `Users` is built, `form_response_body` passes every key of the response, at every level, through the camel-casing helper, skipping keys whose value is None.

models-read-snake-envelope.statement: The ZIdentity list models read the paging fields under the API's own snake_case names: `results_total`, `next_link` and `prev_link`, beside `pageOffset`, `pageSize` and `records`.

envelope-meta-lost.statement: So on the Python list objects (`Users`, `Groups`, `APIClients`, `ResourceServers`) `results_total`, `next_link` and `prev_link` are always None: the keys reach the model as `resultsTotal`, `nextLink` and `prevLink`. `page_offset`, `page_size` and `records` are filled, since those keys have no underscore.
envelope-meta-lost.conditions: Follows from the code path at the pin; none of the three keys is in the helper's exceptions table (searched). The response object's own paging (`has_next`, `next`) reads the raw body and is not affected.

secrets-response-array.statement: Listing an API client's secrets returns a JSON array of secret objects.

secrets-list-into-object.statement: So `get_api_client_secret` returns one secret object whose `id`, `created_at`, `expires_at` and `value` are all None, with no error, instead of the client's secrets: on a list, the key tests never match.
secrets-list-into-object.conditions: Follows from Python membership tests on a list of dicts; not exercised by an SDK test at the pin.

service-entitlement-builds-one.statement: `get_service_entitlement` builds a single `Service` model from the whole response body, and the contract returns service entitlements as an array of objects that each wrap a `service`.

quotes: def get_service_entitlement(self, user_id: str) -> APIResult[dict]:
result = Service(self.form_response_body(response.get_body()))

service-entitlement-into-object.statement: So `get_service_entitlement` returns one `Service` whose fields are all None, with no error, for a user who has service entitlements; the Go SDK's comment describes the same loss when it once read the array into bare service objects.
service-entitlement-into-object.conditions: Follows from the code path at the pin and the contract's array shape; not exercised by an SDK test.

jwks-docstring-key.statement: The Python `add_api_client` docstring takes the JWKS URL as `client_jw_ks_url` in the list under `client_authentication`, and the method sends its keyword arguments as the request body.

quotes:
client_authentication (dict, optional): Configuration details for the client authentication.

                - auth_type (str, optional): The method of client authentication (e.g., "SECRET", "PUBKEYCERT", "JWKS").
                - client_jw_ks_url (str, optional): URL for the JSON Web Keys used for authentication.
body = kwargs

jwks-url-key.statement: So a Python client created as documented sends the JWKS URL as `clientJwKsUrl`, not the contract's `clientJWKsUrl`; the model reads `clientJWKsUrl` back correctly.
jwks-url-key.conditions: Follows from the helper's rule; `client_jw_ks_url` is not in its exceptions table (searched at the pin). Whether the API matches the key case-insensitively is not shown by any source.

group-source-manual.summary: The Python SDK's group docstrings give `MANUAL` as an example group source, which is not in the contract's source values.

positions.says: A group's source is UI, API, SCIM or JIT.

quotes: source (str): The source type of the group (e.g., 'SCIM', 'MANUAL', etc.).

positions.says: Group sources include 'SCIM' and 'MANUAL', among others.

group-source-manual.impact: Code that filters or branches on a `MANUAL` group source never matches; groups made in the console or through the API report `UI` or `API`.

add-group-body.summary: The contract's create-group body defines only `name` and `description`, while the Python `add_group` docstring offers `id`, `source`, `is_dynamic_group`, the two entitlement flags and `idp` as well.

positions.says: A group is created from a name and a description.

quotes: is_dynamic_group (bool): Boolean flag indicating if the group is dynamic.
admin_entitlement_enabled (bool): Whether the group supports admin entitlements.

positions.says: A group can be created with a source, a dynamic flag, entitlement flags and an IdP.

add-group-body.impact: Setting those fields through `add_group` may be ignored or rejected by the API; no source shows which, so read the group back after creating it.
